results.title: Kolmogorov's open map raising dimension
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An interior (open) mapping can raise dimension: there are compact metrizable spaces $X$ and $Y$, where $X$ has small inductive dimension exactly $1$ and $Y$ has small inductive dimension exactly $2$, and a continuous open surjective map $f \colon X \to Y$. A space has small inductive dimension exactly $n$ when its small inductive dimension is at most $n$ but not at most $n - 1$.

results.title: The p-dimensional cube
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For $p \in \mathbb{N}$, the cube $I^p = [0,1]^p$ is the set of points of $\mathbb{R}^p$ all of whose coordinates lie in $[0,1]$, with the subspace topology.

results.title: Open maps can raise the dimension of a cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are natural numbers $p < q$ and a continuous, open, surjective map $f \colon I^p \to I^q$, where $I^p = [0,1]^p$ and $I^q = [0,1]^q$ are the $p$- and $q$-dimensional cubes.

results.title: Unbounded multipliers preserving almost-everywhere convergence to zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of Borel measurable functions $f_n : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f_n(x) \to 0$ for almost every $x \in [0, 1]$. Then there is a sequence of real numbers $(c_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $|c_n| \to \infty$ such that $c_n f_n(x) \to 0$ for almost every $x \in [0, 1]$.

results.title: Decay of dilates of an integrable function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be Lebesgue integrable and let $\lambda > 0$. Then for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $n^{-\lambda} f(nx) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ through the positive integers.

results.title: Heap sort
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $xs$ of elements of a linearly ordered type, heap sort inserts the entries of $xs$ one at a time, from first to last, into the empty binary min-heap, and then extracts the minimum of the heap as many times as the heap has entries, each time continuing with the remaining heap. The output is the list of the extracted minima in the order in which they were extracted.

results.title: Heap sort preserves multiplicities
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $xs$ of elements of a linearly ordered type, the output of heap sort on $xs$ and $xs$ itself are equal as multisets: every value occurs in both lists the same number of times.

results.title: Heap sort permutes its input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $xs$ of elements of a linearly ordered type, heap sort returns a permutation of $xs$.

results.title: Heap sort output is sorted
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $xs$ of elements of a linearly ordered type, heap sort returns a list sorted in nondecreasing order.

results.title: Correctness of heap sort
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $xs$ of elements of a linearly ordered type, heap sort returns a list that is sorted in nondecreasing order and is a permutation of $xs$.

results.title: Residualized vector after adjustment for a subspace
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The adjusted (residualized) `y`: the residual of the least-squares regression of `y` on the subspace `V` (`y` minus its orthogonal projection onto `V`).

results.title: Residuals lie in the orthogonal complement
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Residuals are orthogonal to the adjustment subspace.

results.title: Residuals are orthogonal to every axis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Residuals are orthogonal to every vector of the subspace, in particular to every axis.

results.title: Residual as projection onto the orthogonal complement
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The residual is the orthogonal projection onto `Vᗮ`.

results.title: Additivity of residualization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Residualization is additive.

results.title: Homogeneity of residualization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Residualization is homogeneous.

results.title: Residual vanishes exactly on the subspace
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The residual vanishes exactly on the subspace.

results.title: Stratification within the axis span does not change the residual
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Adding a vector of the subspace (stratification lying in the axis span) does not change the residual.

results.title: Vectors orthogonal to the subspace are their own residuals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Vectors orthogonal to the subspace are their own residuals: stratification outside the axis span is not removed.

results.title: Residual with respect to an orthonormal family of axes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Regressing on an orthonormal family of axes one axis at a time gives the joint residual: `y - ∑ₖ ⟪aₖ, y⟫ aₖ`.

results.title: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem, uniqueness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell, uniqueness: in any least-squares decomposition `y = c + β g + e` with `c ∈ V` and `e ⊥ V ⊔ span {g}`, the coefficient `β` is the coefficient of the regression of the residualized `y` on the residualized `g`, and the residual `e` is the residual of that regression.

results.title: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell theorem, existence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Frisch–Waugh–Lovell, existence: the coefficient of the residual-on-residual regression gives a least-squares decomposition of `y` on `V ⊔ span {g}`.

results.title: EIGENSTRAT association statistic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The EIGENSTRAT association statistic `(N - K - 1) ⟪r_g, r_y⟫² / (‖r_g‖² ‖r_y‖²)` of the adjusted genotype `r_g` and adjusted phenotype `r_y`: `(N - K - 1)` times their squared cosine, which is their squared sample correlation when both are centered (Price et al. 2006). When either adjusted vector is zero the ratio is the junk value `0`.

results.title: Stratification in the axis span is removed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Adding vectors of `V` to the phenotype and the genotype does not change the EIGENSTRAT statistic.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the EIGENSTRAT statistic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The EIGENSTRAT statistic is nonnegative when `K + 1 ≤ N`.

results.title: Genotypes in the axis span carry no signal after adjustment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A genotype lying in the axis span carries no signal after adjustment (its residual is zero, and the statistic is the junk value `0` of the zero denominator).

results.title: Allele-frequency estimate of a marker
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The allele-frequency estimate `p̂ⱼ = μⱼ / 2` of marker `j`, where `μⱼ` is the mean variant-allele count of column `j` (autosomal diploid data, counts in `{0, 1, 2}`).

results.title: Patterson's normalized genotype matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Patterson's normalized genotype matrix `(C i j - μⱼ) / √(p̂ⱼ (1 - p̂ⱼ))`. For a monomorphic marker (`p̂ⱼ ∈ {0, 1}`) the denominator is `0` and the column is the junk value `0`; Patterson et al. use polymorphic markers only.

results.title: Patterson's relatedness matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Patterson's `N × N` matrix `Ψ = M Mᵀ / (number of markers)` of the normalized genotypes, whose top eigenvectors are the axes of variation.

results.title: Patterson's relatedness matrix is positive semidefinite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Patterson's matrix `Ψ` is positive semidefinite.

results.title: All-ones vector lies in the kernel of the relatedness matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The all-ones vector is in the kernel of `Ψ` (columns of the normalized matrix are centered), so at most `N - 1` eigenvalues are nonzero.

results.title: Axes of variation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The axes of variation: an orthonormal eigenbasis of `Ψ`, in decreasing eigenvalue order.

results.title: Eigenvalues of the axes of variation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The eigenvalues of `Ψ` in decreasing order, matching `axes`.

results.title: Span of the top axes of variation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The span of the top `K` axes of variation, the subspace EIGENSTRAT adjusts for.

results.title: Each top axis lies in the span of the top axes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Each of the top `K` axes lies in their span.

results.title: Dimension of the span of the top axes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The top `K` axes span a `K`-dimensional subspace.

results.title: Sequential count of significant axes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Patterson's sequential count of significant axes: among the first `K` statistics, the length of the leading run of statistics exceeding the threshold `t` (testing stops at the first non-significant one).

results.title: At most K axes are declared significant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At most `K` axes are declared significant.

results.title: Characterization of the axes counted as significant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The first `numSignificant stat t K` indices are exactly those `k < K` whose statistics and all earlier ones exceed the threshold.

results.title: Significant axes have statistics above the threshold
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every axis counted as significant has a statistic above the threshold.

results.title: Criterion for at least one significant axis
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At least one axis is significant iff the leading statistic exceeds the threshold.

results.title: Count of significant axes decreases with the threshold
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A higher threshold declares no more axes significant.

results.title: Significant-axis count for decreasing statistics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For decreasing statistics (such as ordered eigenvalues compared with a fixed threshold) the sequential count is the number of statistics above the threshold.

results.title: Conditional error bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If, under the null hypothesis, the `k`-th statistic exceeds `t` with probability at most `1 - F t` (the Tracy–Widom approximation with `F` the TW₁ distribution function, taken here as a hypothesis), then the rule declares more than `k` significant axes with probability at most `1 - F t`.
